title: China’s memory chip makers ride AI boom to new power — and U.S. scrutiny
excerpt: For months, Chinese chip manufacturer ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) had been hiking prices on Huawei, one of the country’s biggest technology companies...
content_html:

(Corrects para 18 to say that CXMT will debut on the market, not launch its IPO)

SINGAPORE, July 24 (Reuters) - For months, Chinese chip manufacturer ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) had been hiking prices on Huawei, one of the country's biggest technology companies. The chipmaker held firm when Huawei demanded relief from the escalating costs, according to two people familiar with the matter.

The standoff came to a head on CXMT's factory floor in June. A group of engineers from a chipmaking-equipment vendor with deep strategic ties to Huawei had been working in the cleanrooms at CXMT's core research and development zone in Hefei, Anhui province. Without warning, CXMT ordered ‌the engineers, who had been helping with equipment maintenance, to pack their tools and leave the factory floor immediately, the two sources said.

Executives at the Huawei-connected equipment vendor, SiCarrier, concluded the confrontation was the result of the power struggle between CXMT and Huawei, the people told Reuters. The companies still do business but the engineers haven't been allowed ‌back into the R&D zone, the two people said.

CXMT, Huawei and SiCarrier didn't respond to questions about the incident.

The clash illustrates the changing dynamics of China's semiconductor industry. CXMT has risen to become the world's fourth-biggest maker of memory, including the DRAM variety used in smartphones, laptops and servers. Now, the company is powerful enough to charge prices even Huawei can't stomach.

Memory chips that help devices run apps and store files were once a low-margin business. CXMT and its ​flash-memory counterpart, Yangtze Memory Technologies Corp, or YMTC, spent years relying on government funding and racking up losses.

But the global buildout of AI data centers has transformed the humble components into one of the world's most sought-after products, sparking battles over pricing and a scramble for supply. The Chinese memory makers are now picking clients and dictating prices, four people familiar with the matter told Reuters. In some cases, they are charging more than their larger South Korean rivals, Samsung and SK Hynix, as skyrocketing demand for memory chips forces Chinese buyers to pay ever-higher prices.

CXMT this month signed a five-year agreement with ByteDance, TikTok's Chinese owner, worth more than $7 billion, three people familiar with the arrangement told Reuters. ByteDance didn't respond to a request for comment about the deal, which hasn't been reported previously.

（更正第18段所说的CXMT将首次上市，而不是启动IPO）

路透新加坡 7 月 24 日 - 几个月来，中国芯片制造商长鑫存储技术有限公司 (CXMT) 一直在提高对该国最大科技公司之一华为的价格。 据两位知情人士透露，当华为要求缓解不断上升的成本时，这家芯片制造商保持了立场。

六月，长鑫存储工厂车间的对峙达到了紧要关头。 一群来自与华为有深厚战略关系的芯片制造设备供应商的工程师一直在安徽合肥长鑫存储核心研发区的洁净室里工作。 两位消息人士称，在没有任何警告的情况下，长鑫存储命令一直在帮助设备维护的工程师收拾好工具并立即离开工厂车间。

知情人士告诉路透社，华为连接设备供应商 SiCarrier 的高管得出的结论是，此次对抗是长鑫存储与华为之间权力斗争的结果。 两人表示，这些公司仍在开展业务，但工程师尚未被允许返回研发区。

长鑫存储、华为和SiCarrier均未回应有关该事件的问题。

这次冲突说明了中国半导体行业动态的变化。 长鑫存储已成为全球第四大内存制造商，其中包括用于智能手机、笔记本电脑和服务器的 DRAM 品种。 现在，该公司的实力已经足够强大，可以收取连华为都无法接受的价格。

帮助设备运行应用程序和存储文件的内存芯片曾经是一项低利润业务。 长鑫存储及其闪存同行长江存储科技公司（YMTC）多年来一直依赖政府资助并不断亏损。

但人工智能数据中心的全球建设已将不起眼的组件转变为世界上最受欢迎的产品之一，引发了定价之争和供应争夺。 四位知情人士告诉路透社，中国内存制造商现在正在挑选客户并决定价格。 在某些情况下，由于存储芯片需求的飙升迫使中国买家支付越来越高的价格，他们的定价高于韩国较大的竞争对手三星和SK海力士。

三名知情人士告诉路透社，CXMT 本月与 TikTok 的中国所有者字节跳动签署了一项为期五年的协议，价值超过 70 亿美元。 字节跳动没有回应有关该交易的评论请求，此前尚未报道过该交易。
